advances: Scalar strict outer tails of a concave width sequence. The mixed-centroid cap transfer has separate geometric premises.

proof:
Trim zero endpoints. The remaining positive support $[\ell,r]\cap\mathbb Z$ is consecutive by concavity, and its mean remains zero. With $N$ the support size, $N=1$ is immediate, $N=2$ cannot have an integer mean, and $N=3$ forces indices $-1,0,1$ and weights $a,b,a$ with $b\ge a>0$. In the last case either $h=0$ and the tails both have mass $(M-m)/2$, or the right-hand side is nonpositive. Hence assume $N\ge4$.

Then $m/M\le1/2$. For $N\ge5$ use the two chords from a maximizing index to height zero at the two ends. If the maximum is interior their sum, with the peak counted once, is $m(N-1)/2$. At an end the single full chord sums to $mN/2$. For $N=4$, after reflection the indices are $-1,0,1,2$. Write the weights as $a,b,c,e$. The mean and concavity give $a=c+2e$ and $c+e\le b\le2c-e$. Thus $M=b+2c+3e$ is at least $2a,2b,2c,2e$: for $2a$ use $b\ge e$, and for $2b$ use $b\le2c-e$. Also $w_0>2m/3$ by fact c46a6b8335f94cab applied to the concave weights with degree one and mean zero.

Fix $h\ge0$, set $k=2h+1$, and suppose the right tail $T=\sum_{i>h}w_i<(M-km)/3$. If $T=0$, the capped first-moment bound of e38bbe8abb5ab718 with cap $m$ and mass $M$ gives $0\le hM-M^2/(2m)+M/2$, a contradiction. Thus $0<T<M/3$. Set $s=h+1$. On the positive support let $F_j=\sum_{i\ge j}w_i$. Fact 108bf10461a9c6ff at degree one makes the actual decrements $\sqrt{F_j}-\sqrt{F_{j+1}}$ nondecreasing for $\ell\le j<r$.

If $s<r$, let $p$ be a maximizing index and put $c_*=m/(2\sqrt M)$. For $p\le s$, the decrement at $p$ is at least $m/(2\sqrt M)$ by its rationalized formula, so every decrement from $s$ on is at least $c_*$. For $p>s$, concavity between $0$ and $p$ gives $w_s\ge w_0>2m/3$, and the decrement at $s$ is greater than $m/(3\sqrt T)>c_*$. Summing only the actual decrements shows $F_{s+v}\le(\sqrt T-vc_*)_+^2$ for all integer $v\ge0$, with the terms beyond $r$ set to zero for this inequality. The distance moment of the right tail then satisfies
$$
E=\sum_{i>h}(i-h)w_i=\sum_{v\ge0}F_{s+v}
\le T+\int_0^\infty(\sqrt T-xc_*)_+^2\,dx
=T+\frac{2\sqrt M\,T^{3/2}}{3m}.
$$
If $s=r$, the same bound holds because $E=T$.

Apply e38bbe8abb5ab718 to the mass $M-T$ on $i\le h$ and add the right-tail moment $hT+E$. The zero mean implies
$$
0\le hM-\frac{(M-T)^2}{2m}+\frac{M-T}{2}+T+\frac{2\sqrt M\,T^{3/2}}{3m}.
$$
With $t=T/M$ and $\mu=m/M$ this gives $k\mu/2\ge (1-t)^2/2-(2/3)t^{3/2}-\mu t/2$. The right side minus $(1-3t)/2$ equals
$$
t\left[\frac5{18}+\frac12(\sqrt t-2/3)^2-\frac{\mu}{2}\right]\ge t/36>0.
$$
Thus $k\mu>1-3t$, contradicting $T<(M-km)/3$. Reflection proves the other tail.
statement:
Let $(w_i)$ be a nonzero nonnegative concave sequence on a finite interval of consecutive integers, with $\sum_i i w_i=0$. Write $M=\sum_i w_i$ and $m=\max_i w_i$. For every integer $h\ge0$,
$$
\min\left\{\sum_{i>h}w_i,\sum_{i<-h}w_i\right\}\ge\frac{M-(2h+1)m}{3}.
$$
For the two sums only, entries off the given index interval are zero.
title: One-third slab-tail bound for a centered concave sequence
